newsitem.title: FRANCE: French star Delon commiserates with jailed Tapie.
newsitem.headline: French star Delon commiserates with jailed Tapie.

text.p: French film star Alain Delon sent a bizarre letter of commiseration on Thursday to bankrupt businessman and former soccer boss Bernard Tapie, in jail for rigging a soccer match.

"Cheer up, Bernard. Jail is tough, I know," Delon, 61, wrote in the open letter to the former chairman of Marseille soccer team and published by the daily Le Figaro. "I stretch out my hand to you through the bars."
Delon, a long-term heart-throb who has played roles ranging from a tough-guy detective to an alcoholic mechanic, used the letter to deplore ills in society ranging from sleaze to child abuse.
"Outside...it's grim. No one is sure of anything or anyone, the frivolous waltzes alongside the shocking. It's sad, very sad, one searches for the least ray of hope," he wrote.

Tapie, who says he is the innocent victim of a political witchhunt in France, has been in jail since February 3, serving an eight-month sentence for rigging a soccer match between Marseille and Valenciennes in 1993.
Delon became embroiled in one of post-war France's biggest scandals in 1968 after the corpse of his ex-bodyguard, Stefan Markovic, was found in a garbage dump outside Paris.

At the time, Delon accused police of "aggressive questioning" and "abusive searches" in a probe that implicated numerous celebrities and politicians and generated rumours that ultimately touched the wife of ex-prime minister Georges Pompidou. The case was never solved.

Delon was not jailed during that investigation but he has recounted several times that he spent his 20th birthday behind bars in a French military prison in Vietnam when he served there in the last stages of France's 1946-1964 Indochina War.
